findings.problem: LedgerWorkflow uses status: String, is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool — invalid state combinations are fully representable (e.g. status="sent" with is_sent=false, status="draft" with is_sent=true, both bools true, validated but not sent, sent but not validated, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: Domain invariant 'sent implies validated' cannot be enforced by the type system; runtime bugs where ledger reaches inconsistent states are silent and unpreventable
findings.fix: Replace status: String, is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool with a single enum typestate (e.g. enum LedgerState { Draft, Validated, Sent { sent_at: u64 } }) that makes every illegal combination unconstructable

findings.problem: id: String is a bare string with no domain identity invariant. Any 0-length, whitespace-only, or malformed string is accepted.
findings.failure_mode: No domain-level validation of ledger identity; invalid IDs propagate silently into the core
findings.fix: Introduce a newtyped LedgerId(String) with a fallible constructor (LedgerId::new) that enforces non-empty, trimmed identity at the boundary

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates in-place (mut item) and returns the struct. No typed error return, no railway programming. The transition from any state to 'sent' is unconditional — no validation gate, no invariant check.
findings.failure_mode: Ledger can be marked sent from any prior state (including invalid/unvalidated states), bypassing the validation gate entirely
findings.fix: Signature: fn mark_sent(item: LedgerWorkflow) -> Result<LedgerWorkflow, LedgerError>. Require the ledger to be in a Validated state before the Sent transition. Return a typed domain error (e.g. LedgerError::NotValidated) if the precondition fails.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent boolean lifecycle flags that can be in inconsistent combinations.
findings.failure_mode: Caller can set both to true (double-transition) or set is_sent=true without is_validated=true, violating the domain invariant that sent ledgers must be validated
findings.fix: Collapse into a single enum typestate that encodes the valid transition graph. The enum variants carry their own data (e.g. Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }) eliminating redundant fields.

findings.problem: status: String stores a free-form string that duplicates information already tracked by is_validated and is_sent. 'sent'.to_string() in mark_sent is redundant with item.is_sent = true.
findings.failure_mode: Status string can diverge from the boolean flags at any point, creating inconsistent observations of the ledger state
findings.fix: Remove status: String entirely. The enum typestate encodes the lifecycle; no separate string field is needed.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> stores raw u64 epoch without any checked conversion at the parse boundary. If this value originates from external input (Unix timestamp, JSON, network), width casts or parse failures are unhandled.
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted epoch values can overflow or come from invalid sources; no boundary validation proven at the type level
findings.fix: Parse at boundaries into a typed EpochMs(u64) with checked conversions. Use u64::try_from with explicit error mapping at the shell boundary.

findings.problem: No typed domain error type exists. mark_sent returns the struct directly with no error path for preconditions (e.g. must be validated before sending).
findings.failure_mode: Precondition violations are either silently ignored or would require panic/expect — both forbidden by Holzman Rust
findings.fix: Define an enum LedgerError { NotValidated, AlreadySent } and return Result<LedgerWorkflow, LedgerError> from mark_sent

findings.problem: All struct fields are pub, allowing external code to mutate state directly without domain methods, bypassing any future invariant checks.
findings.failure_mode: External code can set fields to invalid values without going through typed constructors or transition methods
findings.fix: Make fields private (no pub). Provide constructors and transition methods as the only mutation path.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or any lifecycle transition
no profiler data for allocation patterns in mark_sent (String::to_string + String allocation on status)
no allocation audit — mark_sent calls .to_string() on a string literal (redundant allocation) and the struct fields themselves allocate
no second-ring evidence (no Miri, Kani, or Loom runs to verify state transition invariants)
no command evidence of cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test
residual_risk: Static review only — no commands run. The crate has fundamental typestate violations: illegal ledger states are fully representable via independent bool/string fields. The mark_sent function has no precondition enforcement and no error handling. Without enum typestates and typed domain errors, the core cannot prevent invalid state transitions. The redundant .to_string() on a literal and public fields compound the issues.
